statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 7% (low) with Nasdaq-100 futures inside the CME weekend halt and no live price path available for assessment.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold because no tradable price path can form while index futures are halted until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, seven hours beyond the end of this window. Stress is elevated on a ten-year Treasury yield near a twenty-year high, roughly three-quarters odds priced for an October Fed hike, and a Strait of Hormuz left unresolved by the directly confirmed rejection of Iran's seven-day plan. Easing crude and Iran's stated preference for diplomacy over retaliation on airline sanctions partly offset that, and the first live evidence will arrive only at the Sunday reopen.
headline: Confirmed Hormuz rejection and 20-year-high yields keep Stress elevated while the weekend halt holds Tail at 7
body: Nasdaq-100 index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, seven hours past the 15:00 UTC end of this forecast window, so all twenty-four assessed hours sit inside a closed market. That is the single most important fact for Tail: the pathological price path Tail measures requires a tradable tape, and none exists in this window. Friday's cash session closed constructively and without pathological structure. NDX finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42% or 129.28 points, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and roughly 0.5% below its 30,770.63 52-week high; the S&P 500 added 0.51% to 7,743.41 inside 7,693.08-7,752.07, the Dow rose 0.93% to 51,828.62 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.48% to 27,068.72, capping a week in which the index gained roughly 2%. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87, near the low of its 14.68-15.94 daily range, and gold closed at 4,320.50 dollars. The macro backdrop is the main source of Stress rather than Tail. The Federal Reserve H.15 release puts the two-year Treasury yield at 4.87%, the ten-year at 5.18% and the thirty-year at 5.47%, with the ten-year close to a twenty-year high and the thirty-year mortgage rate at 7.45%, its highest in more than two years. Market pricing carries roughly a three-quarters probability of a 25 basis point hike at the 28 October FOMC, with futures reaching about 4.3% by December against an effective fed funds rate of 3.88%. Under the risk contract that combination compresses multiples and raises the difficulty of the environment without itself denying mean reversion, so it belongs in Stress and Confidence rather than Tail. The geopolitical picture advanced materially since the previous assessment and is now first-hand rather than second-hand. Speaking on camera as he left the White House on Saturday morning, President Trump said he was rejecting Iran's deal, that Iran wanted the strait reopened immediately because it was losing badly, and that the United States has total control of the Strait of Hormuz; he also circulated an image renaming the waterway. Iran's proposal, presented through Qatar at the United Nations General Assembly, had sought a ceasefire on all fronts including Lebanon, removal of the naval blockade, repeal of oil sanctions and release of frozen assets in exchange for reopening the strait on the seventh day and restarting nuclear talks, with President Pezeshkian offering United Nations nuclear inspections. The rejection therefore leaves the waterway closed: IMF PortWatch recorded one transit on 20 September against an 85-a-day pre-crisis baseline, 422 AIS-visible vessels are holding position and CENTCOM has redirected 122 commercial vessels. Against that, the escalation is not uniform. Iran's security council secretary said Tehran would pursue diplomatic negotiations rather than military action over United States airline sanctions, contradicting earlier reporting, while the IRGC continues to vow punishment until Iran's seven conditions are met and Israeli forces struck a Hezbollah weapons storage site in southern Lebanon. Oil eased into the weekend rather than spiking, WTI settling at 92.41 dollars, down 2.33%, and Brent at 104.32, after Iran called on Washington to return to an interim deal. An unresolved waterway with softer crude and a two-sided diplomatic track is weekend gap risk and elevated Stress, not evidence of an imminent pathological price path. One new single-name item belongs in the record: a San Diego jury found that Apple owes Taction a record 5.7 billion dollars over Taptic Engine haptics, and Apple said it does not use the technology and will appeal. Apple closed at 341.07, up 1.53%, and a legal headline of that kind is a reopen consideration for one weight rather than an index-level path. The shared Finviz context read this run is both stale and partial: its generated timestamp is 121 minutes old against the 90-minute freshness limit, and its futures and economic-calendar sections were unavailable, so no delayed cross-asset futures read is claimed here. Its available megacap and semiconductor sections are labelled latest-session with no source as-of and cannot establish current NQ structure; they showed Microsoft up 3.66% on new Copilot capabilities and Qualcomm up 3.97% against Meta down 3.33% after a very strong week and Intel down 3.45%, which reads as rotation rather than the persistent directional efficiency that would justify a higher Tail. Tail is therefore held in a 7-9 band across the window, with the modest late-window rise representing accumulated gap risk ahead of the reopen rather than observed structure, and it never approaches the 25 blocking threshold. Stress runs 47-52, easing slightly through Saturday evening on softer crude and the absence of new escalation, then rising into Sunday as the reopen and a heavy macro week approach: Dallas Fed Manufacturing and a Barkin speech on Monday, JOLTS and consumer confidence on Tuesday, final Q2 GDP with the August PCE price index on Wednesday alongside Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter results after the close, ISM Manufacturing and jobless claims on Thursday, and September payrolls on Friday, where consensus looks for about 90,000 jobs after 162,000 in August with unemployment near 4.1%. Confidence is 82 and decays to 74 across the window. Verified current levels, official yields, oil, volatility, policy pricing, a seven-day calendar and directly sourced geopolitical reporting from within this clock hour are all in hand, which is why Confidence is marginally better than at the previous assessment; what cannot be held, structurally rather than through thin research, is a live price path, and that is what caps Confidence while futures are closed. No danger window is published, because a narrow evidence-based window cannot be justified inside a market that does not trade.
lookbackSummary: All twenty-four preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment. The window opens in the back half of Friday's U.S. session, where Tail ran 18-19 with EA_ON mapped throughout and Stress sat in the mid-50s. After Friday's 21:00Z futures settlement Tail decayed from 12 to 7 and Stress eased from 50 into the mid-40s as the session's directional question closed out, with the mode shifting from mixed to normal and Confidence drifting from 88 down to 81 as the last live observation aged.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forecast hours falls inside the CME weekend halt, which runs until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, seven hours past the 15:00Z end of this window, so no hour can contain observed price-path structure. Tail is held in a 7-9 band throughout; the rise from 03:00Z on Sunday is accumulated gap risk ahead of the reopen, not observed one-way structure, and it stays far below the 25 blocking threshold. Stress runs 47-52, easing through Saturday evening on softer crude and the absence of new escalation, then rising into Sunday as the reopen approaches with the Hormuz question left open by a now directly confirmed rejection and a heavy macro week beginning Monday. The mode is normal while the halt dominates and turns mixed from 09:00Z on Sunday, when two-sided reopen risk becomes the defining hour-specific factor. Confidence decays from 82 to 74 purely through evidence ageing, since no live tape can refresh it. Mapped policy state remains EA_ON in every hour.
